question: The Phase 2 FAQ states the nearest-to-centre rule 'still decides' when regions match equally well, and that Set B deliberately contains pairs where global-argmax disagrees with it. Our shipped Phase 2 path is a bare global argmax. But our generator places targets with NO centre convention (GT nearest-to-centre among GT+decoys in 27.1% of pairs vs 33.0% by chance), so the rule cannot be validated against our labels directly. Does a conservative centre tie-break pay off where the convention happens to hold?
design: Natural experiment, no generator change and no shipped-code change. All 129 decoy-bearing present pairs in p2_val are split by whether the GT is nearest-to-centre among (GT + planted decoys) -- COMPLIANT (n=35) if so, NON-COMPLIANT (n=94) otherwise. Candidates are pooled across all 45 poses, NMS at 0.6x the estimated lattice pitch. The tie-break admits peaks within `margin` of the global peak that are at least 0.75x the lattice pitch apart, then picks the one nearest (500,500); with fewer than two such peaks the global argmax is returned untouched.
decision_rule_preregistered: Ship only if the COMPLIANT slice beats global argmax and the gate fires on less than roughly a third of pairs. Do not ship if the compliant slice is flat or negative, or if the gate fires broadly.
conclusion: REJECTED, including on the slice built to give it the best chance. On the COMPLIANT slice global argmax scores 51.4% and every tie-break margin is worse (45.7 / 48.6 / 40.0 / 28.6% at margin 0.010 / 0.020 / 0.030 / 0.050). Across all 129 pairs argmax scores 31.0% against 25.6 / 24.0 / 17.1 / 10.9%, significant at the wider margins (p=4.0e-05 and p=2.2e-07). The mechanism is visible in the firing rate: the gate fires on 54-89% of pairs even at the tightest margin, because more than half of all pairs have two or more distinct peaks within 0.01 ZNCC of the maximum. The correlation surface over a periodic field is that flat, so an epsilon-margin rule does not arbitrate rare ties -- it overrides nearly every decision, and the centre-most of hundreds of lattice peaks is the true site only 8.3% of the time. No margin helps: tighten it and the gate goes inert, loosen it and accuracy collapses. Phase 1 gates the same rule behind a much narrower wallpaper detector (>=2500 candidates plus a low coarse-context ratio), and that narrowness is evidently load-bearing.
caveats: COMPLIANT slice is n=35, so a 3-pair swing is 8.6 pp; the result is reported as a rejection of a predicted GAIN, which the data does not show at any margin, rather than as a precise effect size.
Compliance is judged against planted decoy geometry, which is a proxy for the organizer convention rather than the convention itself.
p2_val only; no organizer data used.
